title: Repository Instructions
heading: Repository Instructions
text:
Repository Instructions
These instructions apply to every human contributor and AI coding agent, whatever tool is used. `AGENTS.md` files are the only repository instruction source; tool-specific files may only help a tool discover them ([agent instructions](docs/architecture/agent-instructions.md)).

title: Repository Instructions
heading: Global invariants
text:
Global invariants
The repository is the primary source of truth. Keep implementation, schemas, contracts, tests, documentation, and generated artifacts consistent. Do not invent undocumented behavior or treat planned directories and capabilities as implemented.
Use English for source, identifiers, comments, documentation, commit-facing artifacts, database/API descriptions, logs, error codes, tests, scripts, and tooling, except where product localization or external data explicitly requires another language.
Inspect relevant files and existing patterns before editing. Make the smallest coherent change, preserve unrelated work, and explain assumptions that cannot be verified. Prefer the least irreversible solution when uncertain.
Before implementing equivalent UI, inspect existing shared and feature components, metadata and tests under [component reuse practices](docs/architecture/web-components.md#inspect-before-implementing). Reuse matching responsibilities without premature abstraction or speculative component proliferation.
Respect architectural boundaries and accepted ADRs. Search for an existing equivalent before introducing abstractions, dependencies, or cross-layer relationships. Shared code must represent shared meaning. Report architectural conflicts rather than silently bypassing them; significant new decisions require an ADR.
Keep one canonical source where practical. Change sources and regenerate derived artifacts instead of hand-editing generated references. Reviewed SQL migrations follow their separate authorship and release rules.
Preserve [documentation audiences and build isolation](docs/architecture/living-documentation.md#documentation-audiences-and-publication). Internal engineering knowledge remains available in the repository and local portal; product/public documentation requires its own approved sources and application-owned presentation.
Update tests and affected documentation when behavior changes. Never weaken validation, typing, tests, security, or observability merely to make a change pass. Verify at the appropriate boundary and report remaining errors or unavailable checks honestly.
Treat external input as untrusted. Preserve secure defaults and server-side enforcement. Never commit or log secrets, expose internal stack traces to end users, or disable controls for convenience. Expected failures must be explicit and unexpected failures observable.
For implementation work, follow and maintain this repository's implementation plan and human-action checklist, linked from the README's [Current state](README.md#current-state). Update affected task/phase statuses, evidence, and dependencies as work progresses and before handoff; record and surface human blockers instead of silently skipping them. Neither document authorizes work beyond the current task.

title: API-local Instructions
heading: API-local Instructions
text:
API-local Instructions
Read [the runtime guide](README.md) for source locations, local commands, and the module contract. Read the nested `AGENTS.md` of a module before changing it. Global repository instructions still apply.
Preserve `src/main.ts` ordering: parse configuration, initialize Pino/OpenTelemetry, then dynamically load Fastify and compose `src/app.ts` before listening. Instrumented infrastructure depends on this order.
Keep `src/config.ts` as the runtime environment parser. Change schemas and reference metadata together; client-eligible values must pass explicitly through `clientConfigFrom`.
Shared runtime files never import a module. A module implements the `ApiModule` contract in `src/module.ts` and is composed only in `src/modules.ts`; it owns its contracts, errors, routes, persistence adapter, Prisma model file under `prisma/schema/`, metadata under `prisma/metadata/`, runtime grants under `prisma/runtime-grants/`, migrations, tests, and optional process smoke under `scripts/smoke/`.
Keep TypeBox wire schemas/routes at the Fastify boundary. Domain rules and application operations remain independent of Fastify and Prisma; the adapter owns PostgreSQL and conditional writes.
Keep Prisma schema, reviewed SQL, and semantic metadata coherent under [migration](../../docs/database/migrations.md) and [schema-documentation](../../docs/database/schema-documentation.md) policies. The Prisma CLI alone receives `ORION_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`; runtime uses `ORION_DATABASE_URL`.
Generate the ignored Prisma client with root `pnpm db:generate`. For tracked references, follow the [artifact workflow](../../docs/architecture/backend-execution-and-generated-artifacts.md); root `pnpm references:check` includes fresh migrated PostgreSQL and SDK drift checks.
Use allowlisted diagnostics under [redaction policy](../../docs/security/telemetry-redaction.md). Do not attach request bodies, raw URLs, headers, configuration objects, or arbitrary exception messages to logs/spans. Expected failures are explicit; unexpected failures have one authoritative diagnostic event.
Run focused API `test`, `typecheck`, and `build` scripts as applicable, then root `pnpm validate` before substantial-work handoff. Report unavailable checks honestly.

title: API Runtime
heading: Modules
text:
Modules
A module is one cohesive API capability. It implements the `ApiModule` contract in [`src/module.ts`](src/module.ts): a name, an OpenAPI tag, its requirements (`database`, `authentication`), its executable operations, its public error codes, and an `activate` function that mounts routes once its requirements are configured. Shared runtime files never import a module; [`src/modules.ts`](src/modules.ts) is the only composition point, and dependency rules enforce that boundary.
Keep a module's files together under its name: `src/features/<module>/` for domain, application, persistence, contracts, routes, and errors; `prisma/schema/<module>.prisma` for its models; `prisma/metadata/<module>.json` for table meaning; `prisma/runtime-grants/<module>.sql` for least-privilege runtime access; a reviewed migration; tests under `test/<module>/`; and an optional emitted-process smoke at `scripts/smoke/<module>.ts`. Follow [application boundaries](../../docs/architecture/application-boundaries.md), [dependency rules](../../docs/architecture/dependency-rules.md), and the [database policies](../../docs/database/principles.md). [Orion's reference implementation](../../docs/project-derivation.md#orions-reference-implementation) is a complete example.
Outside production, a module whose requirements are not configured stays unmounted. In production, startup fails instead, so a composed capability cannot silently disappear. Generated OpenAPI and the public error registry always include every composed module, whether or not it is configured locally.

Local commands
Use [setup](../../docs/setup.md) for the frozen install, generated Prisma client, environment loading, containers, and startup order. `pnpm -C apps/api dev` loads the ignored root `.env.local` when present; `start` runs emitted code and expects its process environment without loading that file.

Tests and reference generation use fresh migrated Testcontainers PostgreSQL, and identity tests also start the pinned Keycloak image, so a compatible container runtime must be reachable. The root `pnpm validate` also checks emitted builds, real-process recovery, and browser behavior; a focused package check alone does not replace it.

title: API Runtime
heading: Configuration and database access
text:
Configuration and database access
[`config.ts`](src/config.ts) is the sole runtime environment parser; the [generated configuration reference](../../docs/generated/configuration/api.md) owns the setting catalog. `ORION_ENV` is always required. `ORION_DATABASE_URL` enables the database for modules that require it and adds a bounded database check to readiness. `ORION_TOKEN_ISSUER`, `ORION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE`, and `ORION_TOKEN_JWKS_URL` enable bearer authentication and must be configured together.
`ORION_DATABASE_URL` is the restricted runtime credential. Only the Prisma CLI reads `ORION_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`, supplied separately for migration commands; the CLI does not automatically load the API's root `.env.local`. Keep both out of tracked files and do not leave the migration credential in the runtime environment.
The runtime role needs `USAGE` on the application schema plus only the table and column privileges that each module declares in `prisma/runtime-grants/`. It needs no DDL grant. The [database fixture](scripts/migrated-database.ts) provisions separate migration/runtime roles and applies those grants through [`scripts/runtime-grants.ts`](scripts/runtime-grants.ts), so integration tests run with the same least-privilege runtime role. The pilot deployment's release step, [`scripts/release.ts`](scripts/release.ts), applies migrations and the same grants, provisions the realm and ends Keycloak sessions after a restore ([pilot deployment](../../infra/pilot/README.md)).
The [release workflow](../../docs/database/release-evolution.md) owns durable migration recording. An empty registry is not permission to rewrite unverified history.

title: API Runtime
heading: Identity and sessions
text:
Identity and sessions
The [`identity` module](src/features/identity/AGENTS.md) owns application principals and PostgreSQL-backed browser sessions under the [identity and session design](../../docs/project/identity-session-design.md). It requires the database, the token settings and the six `TELUNI_` human identity settings, and stays unmounted outside production until they are configured. Login, callback and back-channel logout are public browser/provider routes under `/auth`; session routes and every product module that needs a human authenticate through its session boundary, exposed to other modules only by `src/features/identity/public.ts`. That boundary passes the stored provider access token through the unchanged verifier below, so the cookie never bypasses it. Bearer-only requests without a session are rejected by session-protected operations.
The realm contract is provisioned by [`scripts/identity-realm.ts`](scripts/identity-realm.ts) and qualified against the pinned Keycloak image in [`scripts/keycloak.ts`](scripts/keycloak.ts). Identity tests start that image and PostgreSQL through Testcontainers.

title: API Runtime
heading: Organizations
text:
Organizations
The [`organizations` module](src/features/organizations/AGENTS.md) depends on the identity session boundary. It owns companies, branches, creator memberships, responsibility, standard-role grants and branch scopes, and append-only organization audit under [D-01](../../docs/project/tenant-data-design.md#implementation-status). Every request resolves current tenant access; administrator and manager grants require strong authentication. Company creation is idempotent per principal/key and atomically creates the creator relationships and audit event. Company and branch changes use expected versions and write audit in the same transaction. Branch and audit pagination reject invalid or incorrectly bound cursors. Runtime grants exclude tenant-column changes, audit edits/deletion and membership/grant administration that has no implemented operation.
The [`mail` module](src/features/mail/AGENTS.md) owns the transactional outbound-email outbox under [ADR-0026](../../docs/adr/0026-propose-a-postgresql-outbox-and-smtp-relay-for-transactional-email.md). It requires the database and the `TELUNI_MAIL_` settings (which also need `TELUNI_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`) and stays unmounted outside production until they are configured. Producers enqueue messages inside their own transactions through `src/features/mail/public.ts`; the dispatcher starts when the server is ready, claims due messages with expiring leases, submits them through SMTP at least once with bounded retries, and stops during shutdown drain.
The `invitations` module, composed from the organizations feature, requires organizations and mail and owns company invitations under [D-13](../../docs/project/invitation-delivery-design.md#implementation-status): administrators and branch managers invite by email, and the person signed in with the invited verified address accepts with the credential from the email link in a request body. Organizations keeps working without it when mail is not configured.
The [two-company suite](test/organizations/integration.test.ts) runs against migrated PostgreSQL as the restricted runtime role; its synthetic session port is confined to the test. The [organizations browser journeys](../web/test/e2e/organizations/companies.spec.ts) use the real identity stack. Platform/support access and bulk operations remain pending in PJ-03/PJ-24.

title: API Runtime
heading: Devices
text:
Devices
The [`devices` module](src/features/devices/AGENTS.md) requires identity, organizations, the database and `TELUNI_DEVICE_CODE_KEYS`, and owns screen enrollment, pairing and lifecycle under [ADR-0027](../../docs/adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md) and the [device enrollment design](../../docs/project/device-enrollment-design.md#implementation-status). A player starts an anonymous enrollment with the hash of a credential it generated, shows the returned code, and polls until a person with `devices.manage` on the target branch claims the code in the panel. Device routes authenticate that credential as a bearer token; check-in renews offline authorization for seven days. Unlinking is irreversible and leaves erasure pending until the device confirms it or a person records a controlled reset. Archiving a branch with active screens is refused with `BRANCH_IN_USE`. A screen may carry an explicit IANA time zone; otherwise it follows its branch, and `GET /device/self` returns the effective zone. The [two-company suite](test/devices/integration.test.ts) covers claims, limits, concurrency, scope, rotation and erasure against migrated PostgreSQL.

title: API Runtime
heading: Media
text:
Media
The [`media` module](src/features/media/AGENTS.md) requires identity, organizations, the database and `TELUNI_MEDIA_STORAGE_PATH`, and owns the company media library under [ADR-0028](../../docs/adr/0028-propose-local-content-addressed-media-storage-and-isolated-ffmpeg-processing.md) and the [media library design](../../docs/project/media-library-design.md#implementation-status). A person with `media.upload` creates an item for the company or one branch, then streams its bytes with `PUT .../content` (`application/octet-stream`, exact declared length); uploads alone may run longer than the standard 30-second request limit. An in-process processor inspects and converts each upload with FFmpeg into a display rendition and a thumbnail, and the item becomes `READY` or `REJECTED` with a reason. Content is served with range support, `nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP. Archive, delete (to a 30-day trash), restore and discard use expected versions; registered reference guards block deleting media in use. FFmpeg/ffprobe 6.1 or later are required; production refuses to start without them. The [two-company suite](test/media/integration.test.ts) processes synthetic media with real FFmpeg against migrated PostgreSQL.

title: API Runtime
heading: Programming
text:
Programming
The [`programming` module](src/features/programming/AGENTS.md) requires identity, organizations, devices, media and the database, and owns playlists, programming groups, the draft programs of groups and screens with their schedule rules, screen assignments and timelines under the [programming design](../../docs/project/programming-design.md#implementation-status) and [ADR-0029](../../docs/adr/0029-propose-temporal-based-schedule-evaluation-with-shared-fixtures.md). Playlists belong to the company or one branch and replace their ordered items as a whole; groups span the whole company or fixed branches; each output's rules are saved as a complete set after wall-clock conflict validation, and a rule check returns conflicting pairs before saving. Timelines evaluate a screen's source in its own time zone (explicit, otherwise its branch's) or a group's program in a chosen zone with the pure evaluator in `schedule.ts`, whose [canonical fixtures](test/programming/schedule-fixtures.json) the player will share. An assignment needs explicit confirmation only while its destination has no publication, which the publications module answers through the programming port. Playlists protect their media from deletion, explicit group spans protect branches from archiving, and a screen moved outside its group's span leaves the group in the move's transaction. It also owns layouts ([`layouts.ts`](src/features/programming/layouts.ts) and [`layouts-service.ts`](src/features/programming/layouts-service.ts)) under the [catalog and composition design](../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#implementation-status): positioned areas on a fixed landscape or portrait canvas, catalog views that bind catalog fields by role, pages that say what each page-controlled area shows, the fit of each view computed with a conservative text measure, and the versioned `teluni.layout` JSON for export and import. It reads catalogs only through the catalogs port and registers a catalogs usage guard and the `layout-draft` media guard, so bound catalogs, fields and named media stay. A program chooses no layout (the single `screen` output) or one layout whose areas are its outputs; dropping outputs with schedules or defaults, by a layout choice or a layout save, needs confirmation, layouts must fit a program's reach, and the programming port gives the publications module a layout snapshot (pagination, catalog records and prices for the branches reached) for protocol 2. The [two-company suite](test/programming/integration.test.ts) runs against migrated PostgreSQL with the real organizations, devices and media modules, and the [layouts suite](test/programming/layouts-integration.test.ts) adds the catalogs module.
The [`publications` module](src/features/publications/AGENTS.md) requires identity, organizations, devices, media, programming, the database and `TELUNI_SYNC_SIGNING_KEYS`, and owns publications, the screen synchronization exchange and screens' synchronization reports under the [publication and synchronization design](../../docs/project/publication-sync-design.md#implementation-status) and [ADR-0030](../../docs/adr/0030-propose-pull-based-screen-synchronization-with-signed-authorization-statements.md). A check builds a program's draft into its publication content and lists what blocks it; publishing needs the content digest the person reviewed and stores the generation's exact manifest bytes, while equal content returns the latest publication. Programs without a layout publish protocol 1; programs with a layout publish protocol 2, with the layout, per-area outputs and catalog snapshots ([catalog and composition design](../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#publication-protocol-2)). Price changes queue one intent per program whose latest publication shows the catalog, and the price publisher (leased, in the API process) publishes the latest generation again with that catalog's current prices after checking its authority again ([automatic price publication](../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#automatic-price-publication)). Screens poll `POST /device/sync` with their device credential, receive the desired publication computed from current rows and an ES256 authorization statement, and download only that publication's manifest and display renditions; reports become each screen's state and 30-day transitions for the panel. Retained publications protect their media from deletion and hourly maintenance prunes those past 90 days. The [two-company suite](test/publications/integration.test.ts) runs against migrated PostgreSQL with the real organizations, devices, media and programming modules and simulated screens.

title: API Runtime
heading: Catalogs
text:
Catalogs
The [`catalogs` module](src/features/catalogs/AGENTS.md) requires identity, organizations, media and the database, and owns typed catalogs, their fields, records, base prices, branch prices and promotions under the [catalog and composition design](../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#implementation-status) and [ADR-0032](../../docs/adr/0032-represent-money-as-integer-minor-units-with-a-currency-per-field.md). A catalog belongs to the company or one branch. Its schema is saved as a whole ordered field list with the catalog version; a field keeps its identifier and never changes type, currency, decimals or reference target, and changes that stored records would break are refused with their count in the error envelope's `issues`. Record values are validated per field type, with money values as integer minor units saved only through the price operations. Promotions use local windows and never overlap for intersecting branches; the effective-price preview applies a promotion, then the branch price, then the base price. Every price change is numbered per catalog in commit order and runs the publications module's listener in its transaction, which refuses it with `PRICE_TARGET_FORBIDDEN` unless the author may publish every program it reaches. Record values protect the media they name from deletion. The [two-company suite](test/catalogs/integration.test.ts) runs against migrated PostgreSQL with the real organizations and media modules.

title: API Runtime
heading: Identity and contract
text:
Identity and contract
The shared [token verifier](src/authentication.ts) accepts verified `at+jwt` tokens signed with RS256 or ES256 by the configured issuer for the configured audience. It validates expiration and requires nonempty `sub`, valid issuance/expiry timing, a stable `orion_principal_id` UUID, `orion_actor_type=human`, and a string `scope`. It yields the principal ID and the issuer-granted scopes; product modules also enforce current session and application-owned memberships. Stored ownership must survive provider changes; request bodies cannot grant identity or capability. The [authentication policy](../../docs/security/authentication.md) and [ADR-0012](../../docs/adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) govern this boundary. Keycloak is selected and locally qualified; no real environment is provisioned.
Executable module contracts own operations, stable operation IDs, typed inputs/outputs, and expected failures. The [OpenAPI reference](../../docs/generated/api/openapi.json) includes health and every composed module's operations; the [error reference](../../docs/generated/api/errors.md) derives from the shared and module registries.

title: API Runtime
heading: Request protection
text:
Request protection
A module that exposes authenticated routes should apply request limiting before token verification and database access, as the reference module does with a process-local source-IP limit; health probes stay outside it. Exhaustion returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` in the public envelope with a bounded `Retry-After`. This is resource protection, not a product quota.
Screen (device credential) routes are the exception to source-IP keying, because many screens share one address behind a store's router or the ingress proxy: [`registerDeviceRequestLimits`](src/device-request-limits.ts) counts each presented credential (a digest, never the credential) on its own under a ceiling of 6,000 requests per address per minute.
Process-local limiting uses the direct peer address; trusted proxies are not configured. A multi-replica or reverse-proxy deployment must define shared/edge limiting and trusted client-IP handling before promising fleet-wide or per-user limits.

title: API Runtime
heading: Lifecycle and diagnostics
text:
Lifecycle and diagnostics
`main.ts` validates configuration, initializes Pino/OpenTelemetry, then dynamically imports Fastify, Prisma, and composed modules before listening. Preserve that order for instrumented infrastructure. Incoming W3C trace context propagates; each request receives a fresh server-generated `x-request-id`. Errors follow the [public envelope](../../docs/api/error-contract.md). Logs and traces identify the service by the API package name.
Startup reports initialization, liveness reports process-local health, and readiness becomes unavailable while draining or when a configured database is unavailable. A configured database is probed before readiness and through a bounded readiness check. SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger bounded HTTP, database, and telemetry shutdown.
Logs and exported spans/metric dimensions use allowlisted operational fields. The runtime does not log payloads, raw URLs, headers, configuration objects, or arbitrary exception messages. Unexpected failures produce one sanitized diagnostic occurrence. A readiness failure or a lost response cannot prove that a prior write failed; see [delivery and side effects](../../docs/architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md).

title: Catalogs Module
heading: Catalogs Module
text:
Catalogs Module
This module owns typed catalogs, their fields, items (records), base prices, branch prices and promotions under the [catalog and composition design](../../../../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md) and [ADR-0032](../../../../../docs/adr/0032-represent-money-as-integer-minor-units-with-a-currency-per-field.md). Read both before changing behavior.
`domain.ts` is pure: field settings, schema planning, value validation, money amounts, promotion overlap and the effective price. Money is an integer count of the field currency's minor units, never a float; numbers are canonical decimal strings. Keep the currency table aligned with `Intl.NumberFormat` (its test fails otherwise) and with the player when protocol 2 lands.
A field's type, currency, decimals and reference target never change; the runtime grants refuse updates to those columns. Schema saves are whole lists with the catalog version; checks that depend on stored items run in the save's transaction and report counts as envelope issues, never values.
Human operations resolve access through the organizations `CompanyAccessPort` and take its `lockForWrite` before any catalog row. Then lock the catalog row (`update` for schema, catalog and order changes and item creation; `share` for item and price writes; `delete` for deletion; `key` for a reference target), then item rows, then media and referenced items. A hidden catalog answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
Item edits need `catalogs.edit` on the catalog's scope and never touch money fields; prices need `prices.edit` on the scope they affect (the catalog's for base prices and scope-wide promotions, the branch's for branch prices and branch promotions), which always needs strong authentication.
Every price write (base price, branch price, promotion creation or deletion) ends with `#priceChanged` in its transaction: it increments the catalog's `catalog_price_sequences` row, which numbers changes in commit order, and runs the registered price change listeners with the branch it reaches (null for the whole scope). A listener's refusal answers `PRICE_TARGET_FORBIDDEN` and rolls the change back, so a price never changes without being queued for the programs that show it ([automatic price publication](../../../../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#automatic-price-publication)).
Item values mirror their media and references into `catalog_record_media` and `catalog_record_references` in the same transaction. The module registers the `catalog-record` media reference guard, which must stay read-only. New media go through the media port's `requireSelectable` and must be images of the company or the catalog's branch.
Other modules use catalogs only through [`public.ts`](public.ts): bindable fields, visibility, view data for previews and protocol 2 publications (read in one repeatable-read snapshot with its price sequence, never under the caller's locks), price sequences, price change listeners and usage guards. A registered usage guard runs inside catalog deletion and schema saves (after the catalog's `update` or `delete` lock) and must stay read-only; a bound catalog answers `CATALOG_IN_USE` on deletion, and a bound field cannot be removed or archived (`FIELD_BOUND` with the count of layouts).
Every change writes its `catalog_audit_events` row in the same transaction, with the branches it concerns; details hold names, field IDs, counts, versions and, for prices, old and new amounts with their currency, never item values.

title: Devices Module
heading: Devices Module
text:
Devices Module
This module owns screen (player) enrollment, pairing and lifecycle under [ADR-0027](../../../../../docs/adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md) and the [device enrollment design](../../../../../docs/project/device-enrollment-design.md). Read both before changing behavior.
The device credential is generated on the device and never reaches the server; only its SHA-256 is accepted, stored and compared. Pairing codes are stored only as HMACs under `TELUNI_DEVICE_CODE_KEYS`. Codes, credentials, hashes and client addresses never reach logs, audit details or error bodies.
Device routes take their pre-authentication limits from `registerDeviceRequestLimits` (per presented credential, under a per-address ceiling); never key them by client address alone, because many screens share one.
Every failed claim, whatever the reason (unknown, expired, already claimed, malformed), answers the same `PAIRING_CODE_INVALID` and counts toward the per-principal and per-company limits.
Human operations resolve access through the organizations `CompanyAccessPort` and take its `lockForWrite` (company, membership and branches `FOR SHARE`) before locking enrollment or device rows; do not add another lock order. A device outside the caller's branches answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
Device rows keep the composite `(company_id, id)` key and never change company; moving changes `branch_id` only. Unlinking is irreversible: the device becomes `REVOKED` with erasure `PENDING`, and only the device's confirmation or a person's reset record ends it.
Each human change and erasure confirmation writes its `device_audit_events` row in the same transaction; details hold IDs and settings only. Other modules import only `public.ts` of identity and organizations.

title: Identity Module
heading: Identity Module
text:
Identity Module
This module owns application principals, server-managed human sessions and the session boundary other modules use. Read the [identity and session design](../../../../../docs/project/identity-session-design.md) and the [identity policies](../../../../../docs/project/identity-and-access.md) before changing behavior.
Other modules import only `public.ts`; dependency rules reject imports of this module's internals. Compose dependents after this module in `src/modules.ts` with `requiresModules: ["identity"]`.
Never weaken the ADR-0012 verifier, the CSRF/Origin check, the 30-second provider revalidation or the single-use login attempt to make a flow pass. A Keycloak behavior that does not meet the design is a recorded gap, not a reason to relax a check.
Keep provider calls outside database transactions, credentials out of logs and errors, and the recoverable cookie credential out of storage (only its SHA-256 digest is persisted; provider tokens are sealed).
The realm contract lives in `apps/api/scripts/identity-realm.ts` and is qualified by `test/identity/keycloak-contract.test.ts` against the pinned image in `scripts/keycloak.ts`; change them together.

title: Mail Module
heading: Mail Module
text:
Mail Module
This module owns the transactional outbound-email outbox, its dispatcher and the SMTP adapter (ADR-0026). Read the [delivery section of the invitation and email delivery design](../../../../../docs/project/invitation-delivery-design.md#durable-email-delivery) and the [delivery policy](../../../../../docs/architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md) before changing behavior.
Producers own what a message means: they register its template and enqueue it through `public.ts` inside their own transaction. Do not add producer-specific wording, rules or tables here.
Delivery is at least once. Never claim exactly once, and keep every outcome write guarded by the claim's lease and the pending state so a stale dispatcher or a cancellation is never overwritten.
Secret parameters stay sealed under the mail key ring and are erased at the final state. Recipient addresses, secrets and message bodies never reach logs, spans, metrics or errors; diagnostics carry message IDs and failure classes only.
Retry timing, attempt limits, lease length and retention live in `domain.ts`; change them with the design, its tests and the schema metadata together.

title: Media Module
heading: Media Module
text:
Media Module
This module owns the company media library: images and videos, their processing into playback renditions, storage and lifecycle under [ADR-0028](../../../../../docs/adr/0028-propose-local-content-addressed-media-storage-and-isolated-ffmpeg-processing.md) and the [media library design](../../../../../docs/project/media-library-design.md). Read both before changing behavior.
Uploaded bytes are untrusted. Admission checks the declared type and size; the processor checks the file signature, forces the matching demuxer and reads files only through FFmpeg/ffprobe child processes started by `ffmpeg.ts` (no shell, PATH-only environment, `-protocol_whitelist file`, timeouts, process-group kill, `prlimit` where present). Never pass user text (names, tags) to a tool, and never log tool output, paths, hashes or file names.
Objects are content-addressed per company under `<root>/objects/<companyId>/` and only `storage.ts` builds paths. Publish an object (insert its row and rename the work file) only inside a transaction holding `lockObject` for that hash. Release one by checking references and deleting the row under that lock, and unlink the file only after the transaction commits, through `removeFiles`/`removeUnrecorded`, which take the lock again and keep the file if the row exists. A purge and an upload of the same bytes then never lose a file, and a rollback never leaves a row without its file; an orphan file is swept.
Human operations resolve access through the organizations `CompanyAccessPort` and take its `lockForWrite` before locking asset rows; then the asset row, then object locks. A hidden item answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. `PURGED` rows stay for audit and are never visible.
Processing claims rows with a lease and an attempt fencing token; every finishing write checks both, so a superseded attempt changes nothing. Rejections are permanent and release the original; failures retry with backoff up to `mediaPolicy.maxAttempts`.
Modules that reference media register a guard through `public.ts` (`registerReferenceGuard`) and select media only through `requireSelectable`. Deletion and purge refuse while any guard reports a reference. Each human change writes its `media_audit_events` row in the same transaction; details hold IDs, sizes and settings only.

title: Organizations Module
heading: Organizations Module
text:
Organizations Module
This module owns companies (tenants), branches, memberships, standard role and access profile grants, the responsible administrator and organization audit. Read the [tenant data design](../../../../../docs/project/tenant-data-design.md) and the [permission matrix](../../../../../docs/project/identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix) before changing behavior.
Every tenant-owned table with its own `id` keeps `(company_id, id)` unique and every tenant reference composite; the structural suite in `test/organizations/integration.test.ts` enforces it on the migrated schema. Join tables and one-to-one extensions without an `id` follow D-01's key exception. Never grant runtime `UPDATE` on `company_id` or `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on audit events.
Resolve access on every request through `OrganizationService.access`; never cache it beyond the 30-second revocation bound, and never take company, branch or role from a request body as authority. Hidden resources answer `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
Role capabilities live in `domain.ts`; administrator and branch-manager grants count only in strongly authenticated sessions (P12). Add a capability with the module that needs it, not speculatively.
Authority-changing writers lock the company row first, then the involved memberships in ID order, and recheck the actor's current membership and grants inside that transaction (tenant data design rule 5). Reuse `lockAuthority` in `prisma-repository.ts` for grant, status and responsibility writes; invitation writes lock the company, then the invitation, then memberships, and rebuild the actor's access inside the transaction. Do not add another lock sequence. Modules writing tenant data under the company's authority (such as devices) take `lockForWrite` through `CompanyAccessPort`, which holds the company, the actor's membership and the named branches `FOR SHARE`. Work a member authorized earlier and the API effects later (automatic price publication) takes `lockForMembership` instead, which rechecks that membership and rebuilds its access from current grants, counting strong authentication as proven; never use it for a person's request. Branch archive runs registered guards so such modules can refuse it with `BRANCH_IN_USE`.
Access profiles (`profile-repository.ts`) combine only `delegableCapabilities` from `domain.ts`; never make administration, settings, branch or member management delegable. A profile's assurance is per capability (`strongCapabilities`), never per label. Resolve a profile's current capabilities on every request; profile writes follow the same lock order, and each edit audits its added and removed capabilities and affected grants.
Grants are added and revoked, never edited in place. Granting company administration and proposing or accepting a responsibility transfer require the responsible administrator (or, for acceptance, the proposed successor) with strong authentication no older than five minutes, checked against the database clock inside the transaction.
Each change writes its audit event in the same transaction, passing to `writeAudit` the branches the event concerns (none for company-level events); branch managers read only events confined to their branches. Member presentation data comes only from identity's `HumanProfilePort` for principals on an authorized page. Other modules import only `public.ts`.
Invitations (`invitation-*.ts`, composed as the separate `invitations` module) follow the [D-13 design](../../../../../docs/project/invitation-delivery-design.md). Never look up principals by email; only the accepting session's verified email binds an invitation. Credentials are stored only as hashes, travel only in request bodies and never reach logs. Each invitation and its email commit in one transaction through the mail outbox, and acceptance revalidates the inviter's current authority without narrowing the grant.

title: Programming Module
heading: Programming Module
text:
Programming Module
This module owns playlists, programming groups, the draft programs of groups and screens, schedule rules, screen assignments and timelines under the [programming design](../../../../../docs/project/programming-design.md) and [ADR-0029](../../../../../docs/adr/0029-propose-temporal-based-schedule-evaluation-with-shared-fixtures.md). Read both before changing behavior.
`schedule.ts` is pure: it never reads a clock or the process time zone and takes IANA zone names explicitly. Keep conflict validation in local wall-clock minutes and zone resolution (gaps to the transition instant, repeated hours earlier for starts and later for ends, then the handoff clip) in the evaluator. Every behavior change updates the canonical [fixtures](../../../test/programming/schedule-fixtures.json), which the player (PJ-12) also runs; never change an expected result to make a test pass. `zoneOffsets` describes a zone with the same rules for screens, which resolve local times against it ([player design](../../../../../docs/project/player-design.md#trusted-time-and-zone-offsets)); after changing the fixtures or zone handling, regenerate the player conformance file with `pnpm -C apps/api conformance:write`.
Human operations resolve access through the organizations `CompanyAccessPort` and take its `lockForWrite` before any programming row. Then lock in this order: screen rows (through the devices port's `describe` with a transaction), settings, groups, layouts, programs, the per-company limits lock that `counts` takes before every count-and-insert, playlists. A resource the caller can see only partly, such as a group spanning a branch outside their reach, answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; a screen's views show such a group as `null` and such a playlist by its ID only.
A rule or default may use a playlist only when every branch its program can reach is inside the playlist's scope; new media in a playlist must be selected through the media port's `requireSelectable` and fit the playlist's scope.
The module registers the `playlist-draft` media reference guard, the branch archive guard for explicit group spans and the devices move hook. They run inside the other module's transaction and must stay read-only, except the move hook, which updates the screen's settings in the move's transaction.
Layouts follow the [catalog and composition design](../../../../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#layouts). `layouts.ts` is pure and holds the layout rules, the `teluni.layout` document and the conservative text measure that screens' renderer must never exceed; changing the measure or a limit changes what fits on screens, so update the design and its fixtures with it. After the company access, layout writes lock the layout row (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE` for saves, `FOR UPDATE` for deletion) or take the limits lock (creation), then the programs that use the layout, then bound catalogs through the catalogs port's `requireBindable` (`FOR KEY SHARE`), then new media through the media port. A program operation that reads its layout share-locks the layout before the program, so layouts always lock before programs. Saves replace the whole definition, so an area's key is its only identity: the API keeps keys exactly as given and never renames them, and a key left out removes that area. Program outputs are keyed by area keys (`screen` for a program without a layout), so a layout choice or save that drops outputs with schedules or defaults, or the default of an area that becomes a catalog area, answers `LAYOUT_CHANGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` until confirmed, under the design's [programs with layouts](../../../../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#programs-with-layouts); the panel keeps saved keys read-only. A program's layout must fit its reach like a playlist (`LAYOUT_SCOPE_MISMATCH`), including after span changes, and a layout that programs use cannot be deleted. The publications module publishes programs with a layout as protocol 2 from `publicationSnapshot`, and re-prices a published copy with `repriceCatalog`, which keeps the copy's records and paginates its views again with the same measure. The module registers the catalogs usage guard and the `layout-draft` media guard; both must stay read-only.
Assignments never edit programs. An assignment needs `confirmUnpublished` only when its destination has no publication, which the publications module answers through `onPublicationFacts`.
Every change writes its `programming_audit_events` row in the same transaction, with the branches it concerns; details hold names, counts, versions and IDs only.

title: Publications Module
heading: Publications Module
text:
Publications Module
This module owns publications (immutable generations of programs), the screen synchronization exchange, manifest and media delivery to screens, signed authorization statements and screens' synchronization reports under the [publication and synchronization design](../../../../../docs/project/publication-sync-design.md) and [ADR-0030](../../../../../docs/adr/0030-propose-pull-based-screen-synchronization-with-signed-authorization-statements.md). Read both before changing behavior.
A stored manifest is the exact bytes screens receive and statements sign; never rebuild or re-serialize a stored manifest. Manifests and content digests come only from `domain.ts`: protocol 1 for programs without a layout, byte for byte, and protocol 2 for programs with one ([catalog and composition design](../../../../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#publication-protocol-2)). A format change is a new protocol, served beside the old one for the support window.
Protocol 2 content comes only from the programming port's layout snapshot, taken under the program's locks; it carries prices for the branches the program reaches, so a restore never serves a wider reach.
A screen's desired publication is computed from current rows at each request (its programming source through the programming port, then that program's latest publication); never store or fan out desired state, and never trust a reported publication ID beyond resolving it within the screen's company.
Manifests and media are delivered only for the screen's current desired publication. Statements list the desired publication and, while it is not active, the reported active and recovery ones that are unpruned publications of the same company; an unpublished source lists none.
Human operations resolve access through the organizations `CompanyAccessPort`, take its `lockForWrite` with the program's branches, then let the programming port share-lock the source, program and playlists and the media port share-lock the media, and only then take the per-company publication lock (`lockCompany`). The price processor follows the same order with `lockForMembership` for the intent's authority. Do not add another lock order.
Automatic price publication follows the [catalog and composition design](../../../../../docs/project/catalog-composition-design.md#automatic-price-publication). The price change listener runs in the catalogs module's transaction: it takes the publication lock shared (`lockPublicationsShared`), so every publication sees a change committed before it, and it only reads and queues. A protocol 2 publication records its catalog copies with their price sequences, settles the intents they include and queues changes the copies missed; never publish a catalog's prices outside `#record`. The processor copies the latest generation (`price.base`), never drafts, rechecks the authority's `publications.publish` on the program, and finishes its intent in the same transaction under its lease.
Each publication, restore or price publication writes its `publication_audit_events` row in the same transaction. Signing keys, manifests, statements and credentials never reach logs, audit details or error bodies.
Screen routes take their pre-authentication limits from `registerDeviceRequestLimits` (per presented credential, under a per-address ceiling); never key them by client address alone, because many screens share one.
The `publication` media guard, the programming port's publication facts and the price change listener run inside other modules' transactions, must query through that transaction (the listener writes only intents), so they keep protecting media and assignments and queueing price changes while this module is unmounted.
The sync answer's `zoneOffsets` come only from the programming port's `zoneOffsets`, the zone rules its evaluator uses, so screens agree with the preview ([player design](../../../../../docs/project/player-design.md#trusted-time-and-zone-offsets)). The player reads `test/publications/conformance.json`; when the manifest, statements or zone rules change, regenerate it with `pnpm -C apps/api conformance:write` in the same change.

title: Player Instructions
heading: Player Instructions
text:
Player Instructions
Read [the player guide](README.md) for layout and commands, and the [player design](../../docs/project/player-design.md) and [ADR-0031](../../docs/adr/0031-build-the-player-on-a-portable-core-with-file-based-atomic-state-and-managed-installation.md) before changing behavior. Global repository instructions still apply.
Every rule lives in `core`, which stays free of Android dependencies so the JVM tests cover it. The future `app` module adapts the platform (clock, storage location, Keystore, rendering) to `core`'s interfaces and holds no rule of its own.
The player is an untrusted client of the published device contracts. Never import or copy backend or web code. Keep the wire models in `core/.../sync/DeviceApi.kt` in step with the [OpenAPI document](../../docs/generated/api/openapi.json); `ContractTest` fails when a field name differs.
Business time never comes from the device's time zone data: resolve local times only with the server's `zoneOffsets`, and take "now" only from `TrustedClock`. The evaluator mirrors the API's evaluator. Change both together with the [shared fixtures](../api/test/programming/schedule-fixtures.json) and regenerate the [conformance file](../api/test/publications/conformance.json) with `pnpm -C apps/api conformance:write`; never edit an expected result to make a test pass.
Protected output needs a verified, unexpired statement that lists the playing generation. Never extend a statement's expiry, trust an unverified one, or play content outside the active generation.
Writes go through `AtomicFiles`: temporary file, flush, rename, directory flush. Media enter the store only after their length and SHA-256 match. Changing the state record's format needs a forward migration or a re-synchronization that keeps the credential, and tests for both.
Credentials, statements, manifests, media and pairing codes never reach logs, exceptions shown to people or reports.
Pin new dependencies in the version catalog, then refresh `gradle.lockfile` and `gradle/verification-metadata.xml` in the same change (see the README). Run `./gradlew check` (or the preinstalled Gradle where the wrapper cannot download) before handing off.

title: Teluni Android TV Player
heading: Teluni Android TV Player
text:
Teluni Android TV Player
The screen application of the [player design](../../docs/project/player-design.md) under [ADR-0020](../../docs/adr/0020-propose-a-native-android-tv-player.md) and [ADR-0031](../../docs/adr/0031-build-the-player-on-a-portable-core-with-file-based-atomic-state-and-managed-installation.md). It is a Gradle build outside the pnpm workspace, so `pnpm validate` does not build it. The **Player** CI job checks it on every pull request as part of the required gate.

title: Teluni Android TV Player
heading: Current state
text:
Current state
`core` holds the portable rules. The Android `app` adds a TV activity, code-based enrollment, an AES-256-GCM Android Keystore vault, a foreground synchronization service, Media3 image/video rendering, protocol 2 areas and catalog views, rotation, neutral output and device-owner HOME/lock-task integration. Debug and unsigned release APKs can be built. Local emulator verification is recorded in the [implementation status](../../docs/project/player-design.md#implementation-status); it does not qualify physical hardware or the release/update channel.
Package in `core/src/main/kotlin/app/teluni/player/core/`
Responsibility
`schedule/`
The schedule evaluator ported from the API, rule validation, and resolution of local times against the zone offsets the server sends
`protocol/`
Strict parsing and checks of protocol 1 manifests and of protocol 2 manifests with layouts and catalog snapshots (another protocol is refused as incompatible), and ES256 statement verification with Nimbus JOSE + JWT
`catalog/`
Effective prices of protocol 2 catalogs, ported from the API
`time/`
Trusted time: a monotonic anchor from each sync, a persisted lower bound, and the system clock after a reboot only when it is plausible
`store/`
App-private storage: atomically replaced records, exact manifests and write-once media named by SHA-256
`sync/`
The device API over OkHttp, and the engine for enrollment, synchronization, staging with resumable verified downloads, activation, recovery, stored-media integrity checks and erasure
`playback/`
What plays now and until when, or which neutral output and why; for a layout, what each area shows, with the coordinated page cycle, catalog view pages and prices for the screen's branch
The running app re-hashes one referenced media file at a time on a background-priority worker, starting after 10 seconds and then every 60 seconds. Decoder/image failures request a check of the affected file on that worker. A missing, unreadable or mismatched file is excluded from output and deleted; intact playlist items, layout areas and catalog text remain available with `DEGRADED` status. If that generation is still desired, the next synchronization repairs only the missing media, retaining its original activation time and recovery generation. Intact bytes rejected by a decoder are not downloaded repeatedly. Per-file repair revisions reopen affected media even when the repair finishes between rendering ticks; intact catalog text keeps its views while changed bitmaps refresh in place. Checks serialize with staging and stop for erasure; startup keeps its existing presence/size checks for fast cached output. Device qualification remains PH-08.
Player health reports include the clock reference, signed system skew against an anchor and the number of uncaught crashes recorded during this pairing. Unknown values remain unknown. Crash messages, causes, filenames and foreign frames are excluded; the latest bounded player code frames stay in app-private storage and only the count is sent. Enrollment/erasure delete the evidence. Earlier versions' unrecorded failures are not reconstructed. The panel's screen detail labels these as reported facts and highlights system skew above 60 seconds; playback and signed authorization still use trusted time. Apply the [diagnostic migration and API before updating players](../../docs/project/player-design.md#diagnostics-and-privacy).

title: Teluni Android TV Player
heading: Build and checks
text:
Build and checks
Use JDK 17 and the Android SDK (`ANDROID_HOME`): platform `platforms;android-37.0` and build tools `build-tools;36.0.0`. The runtime floor remains Android 8/API 26; supported pilot hardware has its separate [envelope](../../docs/project/player-design.md#supported-hardware-envelope). From this directory:
./gradlew --no-daemon check :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleRelease

`check` runs core tests, Android adapter/UI tests with Robolectric (API 35 on JDK 17) and Android lint. Debug output is `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`; the unsigned release is `app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk`. Release signing is not configured: PH-27 remains open. `pnpm validate` checks the rest of the repository, separately from this Gradle gate.
The core tests consume the API-owned [schedule fixtures](../api/test/programming/schedule-fixtures.json), [protocol conformance file](../api/test/publications/conformance.json) and [OpenAPI document](../../docs/generated/api/openapi.json). Robolectric's Android platform is also a pinned, locked and checksum-verified Gradle dependency; its runtime is offline after resolution.
The wrapper pins Gradle 9.6.0 and its SHA-256, with Android Gradle Plugin 9.4.1 and Media3 1.11.1 in the [version catalog](gradle/libs.versions.toml). Refresh dependency locks and verification metadata together, review the complete diff, then run again without write flags:
./gradlew --no-configuration-cache --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 :core:dependencies :app:dependencies check :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleRelease
./gradlew --no-daemon check :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleRelease

Use a fresh Gradle cache when auditing metadata completeness. Do not disable dependency verification to resolve a build failure.

title: Teluni Android TV Player
heading: Local emulator
text:
Local emulator
Android Studio is optional. Install JDK 17 and Google's command-line tools, then install these SDK packages (the current Android CLI uses `/` separators; legacy `sdkmanager` uses `;`):
android sdk install platforms/android-37.0 build-tools/36.0.0 platform-tools emulator system-images/android-36/android-tv/x86_64

Create an AVD named `teluni-tv-api36` with the Android TV x86_64 image and the `tv_1080p` device profile. With the legacy AVD manager:
avdmanager create avd -n teluni-tv-api36 -k 'system-images;android-36;android-tv;x86_64' -d tv_1080p

Start the [local API and panel](../../docs/setup.md), then run from the repository root:
pnpm player:dev

The command builds the debug APK, opens the emulator if needed, waits up to four minutes for startup, installs the APK and opens the player. It never provisions device ownership, resets an emulator or erases player data. `ANDROID_HOME`, `JAVA_HOME`, `GRADLE_USER_HOME`, `ANDROID_SERIAL` and `TELUNI_PLAYER_AVD` override its local defaults. Without overrides it looks in `~/.local/share/teluni-android-sdk`, `~/.local/share/teluni-toolchains/jdk17` and `~/.cache/teluni-player-gradle`, using `emulator-5554` and `teluni-tv-api36`. The emulator needs KVM access and a graphical desktop; software graphics are selected for reproducible local testing.
On the setup screen, choose **Connect** with the remote/keyboard. The debug default `http://10.0.2.2:3000` reaches the host API through the Android Emulator's host alias. In the host browser, open the panel at `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, choose a company and branch, then **Screens → Pair screen** and enter the displayed code. Assign a published program through the screen's programming page. The player downloads, verifies and activates it automatically. Use arrows and Enter as the TV remote; OK/Enter during playback displays a status card for 30 seconds.
Changing media, playlists or schedules in the panel requires publication before screens receive them. A configured, paired player restores its cached generation and credential after a process restart; offline output remains bounded by the verified authorization and trusted clock. Basic installation stays outside the physical unattended-operation qualification.
To reset only a disposable test player's data (this erases its identity and cached content):
adb -s emulator-5554 shell pm clear app.teluni.player

Unlink the previous screen in the panel before pairing a new identity. Do not reset a real pilot device as a testing shortcut.

title: Teluni Android TV Player
heading: Configuration and security
text:
Configuration and security
The app owns one operator-entered, non-secret API endpoint, validated by `PlayerEndpoint` at setup and startup. It is stored atomically in app-private `endpoint.txt`, is client-visible and contains no authentication material. No default is supplied in release builds. The address must be HTTPS, without user information, query or fragment; a paired installation keeps its endpoint until its data is deliberately erased. No API server secrets or human tokens are embedded in the APK.
Only debug builds allow HTTP for `10.0.2.2`, `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`, enforced both by the parser and a debug-only network security resource. Release builds require HTTPS and system certificate validation. There is no global cleartext or certificate-validation bypass.
Device credentials are generated by core and encrypted with a non-exportable Android Keystore AES key. Backup and device transfer are disabled. An unreadable credential causes core to discard the old identity and content. Pairing codes are displayed only during enrollment; telemetry records bounded error codes, without credentials, statements, manifests, media, pairing codes or raw exception messages. Crash diagnostics contain only player stack frame names/line numbers in the private `diagnostics/last-crash.txt` file.

title: Teluni Android TV Player
heading: Managed installation
text:
Managed installation
Use a factory-reset, explicitly designated pilot/test device with no accounts. Install the appropriately signed APK through `adb`, then provision the player as device owner:
adb shell dpm set-device-owner app.teluni.player/.PlayerAdminReceiver
adb shell am start -n app.teluni.player/.PlayerActivity

The app checks actual device ownership before allowlisting itself for lock task and registering its persistent HOME activity. It never tries to grant itself ownership. The boot receiver launches only that owner profile; normal sideloads remain ordinary apps. Do not factory-reset a device merely to try this command. The release key (PH-27), update distribution, credential rotation and physical boot/crash/power-loss qualification (PH-08) remain pending.

title: Web Application Instructions
heading: Web Application Instructions
text:
Web Application Instructions
Use [the web guide](README.md) for source locations, startup, and browser checks. Global repository instructions still apply.
Product workflows use the generated workspace SDK (`packages/sdk`) as the API boundary. The generic documentation explorer follows its [bounded OpenAPI execution contract](../../docs/architecture/living-documentation.md#safe-local-reading-and-api-exploration). Change API TypeBox contracts and regenerate OpenAPI/SDK through the [artifact workflow](../../docs/architecture/backend-execution-and-generated-artifacts.md); never import API implementation or hand-edit generated types.
Keep URL-owned list scope/cursor and detail IDs in TanStack Router, API-owned state in TanStack Query, and temporary form state in React. Clear cached query data when the in-memory bearer token changes and on sign-out. Never store the session cookie, CSRF token or provider tokens in URLs, storage or logs.
Browser input and UI visibility do not grant permission. Preserve visible authorization denials, stale-version conflicts, idempotency, and unknown-outcome recovery that a module's API defines, without reimplementing business rules in React. Compose module routes and navigation only in `src/modules.tsx`.
`VITE_ORION_API_BASE_URL` is the only public API setting and must be a same-origin path. Keep credentials in memory, never URLs, storage, logs, or generated artifacts; server/development proxy targets remain outside browser configuration.
Maintain exported component examples/metadata beside source under [living documentation ownership](../../docs/architecture/living-documentation.md); regenerate portal data and component Markdown rather than editing generated files.
Before adding equivalent UI, follow [inspect-before-implementing](../../docs/architecture/web-components.md#inspect-before-implementing): search the shared entry point, root/feature metadata, generated catalog and relevant private source/tests. Choose native/local UI when reuse does not match. Classify documented components by category, owner and reuse scope; every public shared component export needs metadata, while private helpers do not. Keep domain behavior in features and use product-owned semantic styling tokens.
Keep internal portal imports behind the [build boundary](../../docs/architecture/living-documentation.md#build-and-deployment-boundary). Preserve the default production exclusion and its tests. Product layouts, branding, routes, and help remain application-owned; internal build selection never grants access or API permissions.
Run focused `typecheck`, `build`, `bundle:check`, unit/browser/end-to-end checks as applicable, then root `pnpm validate` before substantial-work handoff. See [validation](../../docs/validation.md) for prerequisites and limits.

title: Web Application
heading: Modules
text:
Modules
A web module is the browser side of a product capability. It defines its routes as children of the shared root route, keeps its pages, client calls, styles, and wording in its own `src/<module>/` folder, and exports a navigation link component. [`src/modules.tsx`](src/modules.tsx) is the only composition point: it adds the module's routes to the route tree and its links to the shell navigation and home page. Shared shell and portal code never import a module. Module browser journeys belong in `test/e2e/<module>/` and may start their own disposable stack with the shared [end-to-end stack helpers](test/e2e/stack.ts). [Orion's reference implementation](../../docs/project-derivation.md#orions-reference-implementation) is a complete example.
Use the shared [`ErrorNotice`](src/components.tsx) and [`api-client.ts`](src/api-client.ts) for public API failures: pass a module's own stable codes when unwrapping responses and its own wording for them. A failed or lost write is an unknown outcome, never proof that nothing changed.

title: Web Application
heading: Entry and home page
text:
Entry and home page
Teluni composes its own `/` route from the [`workspace` web module](src/workspace/routes.tsx) instead of the shell's generic home page. A visitor without a session (or when the session service is unavailable) goes to `/sign-in`; a signed-in person sees the home page with their first companies, a path to create the first company, and the session's two-step verification state. `/sign-in` sends a signed-in person on to `returnTo` or the home page, and presents the product beside the sign-in action. The sidebar shows Home, Companies, the session entry and, in development only, Documentation.
The Living Documentation Portal is a development aid, not part of the product (owner direction, 2026-10-19). [`src/modules.tsx`](src/modules.tsx) uses the foundation's `__ORION_INTERNAL_DOCS__` build boundary: the development server serves `/docs`, while default production builds drop the routes, portal code and generated pages. The Vite isolation plugin rejects accidental internal imports; [`scripts/check-public-bundle.mjs`](scripts/check-public-bundle.mjs), part of `bundle:check`, additionally checks Teluni's distributed product artifact. Explicit protected internal builds follow the foundation policy below and are never pilot/public artifacts.

title: Web Application
heading: Identity
text:
Identity
The product shell follows the [Connected Tiles interface plan](../../docs/project/implementation-plan.md#pj-41-interface-alignment): desktop navigation is a sidebar and mobile navigation is a disclosure controlled by Menu, with Escape returning focus to the trigger and route selection closing it. Existing modules still own their links and permission checks. The [`CompanyNavigation`](src/organizations/navigation.tsx) contribution, composed in `src/modules.tsx`, adds the current company's name, a link to switch companies through the existing company list, and links to its available workflows throughout that company's routes. The home page uses the existing company list and account state without adding synthetic counts or activity.
Company context comes exclusively from the matched route's `companyId`; no company ID is persisted or inferred from a query parameter. The navigation shares the existing company-detail query and server-returned effective capabilities with product pages. Role names and capabilities that require further step-up do not make links available. Pending/error access, including a failed refetch that retains old cached data, hides company links; switching companies uses a separate query key without keeping the previous company's data visible. Company view selection follows the URL while ignoring pagination for the selected view, and changing views clears the cursor. The developer portal makes no session/company requests. [`company-navigation.spec.ts`](test/e2e/company-navigation.spec.ts) qualifies context switching, current-section selection, restricted capabilities, desktop/mobile themes and portal isolation; browser component coverage also checks cached access revocation.
[`tokens.css`](src/tokens.css) owns semantic colors and shared spacing/radius values; [`shell.css`](src/shell.css) owns the product structure. Existing product controls, cards and status notices consume those colors. The Theme selector offers System, Light and Dark. System is the default and follows live `prefers-color-scheme` changes; an explicit choice stores only `teluni.theme=light|dark` in local storage, synchronizes across tabs and persists across reloads. Returning to System removes the key. Invalid stored values fall back to System, and unavailable storage leaves selection usable for the current view. No session, credential or tenant information is stored with appearance. Theme state is scoped to the product shell, so the developer portal retains its existing light presentation without reading the preference. The separate Keycloak pages retain their own branded light theme.
The product shell maps the foundation's inherited `--ui-*` component hooks to these canonical Teluni tokens. Shared Button, TextField and ErrorNotice therefore follow the product's typography, colors, focus and light/dark appearance. Feature forms and business state remain locally owned; adopting the reference set does not replace the existing workflows.
The first PJ-41 increment qualifies home, company entry/forms, denial and sign-in surfaces in both themes, with browser coverage in [`shell.spec.ts`](test/e2e/shell.spec.ts). Company navigation extends the sidebar through company workflows. The device increment adopts the shared controls in pairing and lifecycle forms, retains native confirmation and domain-owned recovery, and adds detailed theme/responsive coverage in [`device-interface.spec.ts`](test/e2e/device-interface.spec.ts). An unknown pairing response requires an explicit list reload before another submission. Remaining modules' detailed states, visual refinement and provider appearance are tracked by PJ-41; shared token adoption alone does not complete that task.
The display name comes from `.orion/project.json` at build time: page titles, the shell brand, and the portal show the repository's own name. The [brand mark](src/assets/brand-mark.svg) and its derived [touch icon](src/assets/brand-touch-icon.png) belong to the repository. The Orion foundation uses the Orion mark; project initialization replaces both files with a neutral placeholder for the project to redesign.
The shell, documentation navigation, and browser favicon consume the SVG directly. Only the Apple touch icon uses a derived 180×180 PNG on the approved `#F8FAFC` light background. After editing the SVG, run `pnpm -C apps/web identity:write` to regenerate that raster through the [export script](scripts/generate-touch-icon.mjs), using the Playwright Chromium installation described in [setup](../../docs/setup.md#prepare-a-clean-checkout). Commit both files, then rebuild. Do not edit the PNG independently. Adjacent live text names the decorative mark for accessibility.
Teluni uses the owner-approved [Connected Tiles identity](../../docs/project/branding/README.md): the selected symbol, a locally served Plus Jakarta Sans variable font with its OFL notice, titlecase live brand text, and blue/teal/navy palette. The runtime SVG is canonical, and `identity:write` derives its touch PNG. The branding guide owns the single identity kit and remaining domain/trademark evidence.

title: Web Application
heading: Run the application
text:
Run the application
Use the canonical [setup guide](../../docs/setup.md) for installation, environment loading, and prerequisites. For an API at `127.0.0.1:3000`, run `pnpm -C apps/web dev`.
Vite forwards the default `/api` browser path to the local API and removes that prefix. `ORION_WEB_API_TARGET` changes only the development-server target. `VITE_ORION_API_BASE_URL` is the sole browser API setting, defaults to `/api`, and must be a same-origin path. A deployed static build needs an equivalent same-origin route/reverse proxy; this guide does not select deployment infrastructure. Server-only URLs and credentials must not enter browser configuration.
Human sign-in uses the server-managed session of the API's `identity` module. The [`identity` web module](src/identity/routes.tsx) provides `/sign-in`, `/account/sessions` and the shell's sign-in/sign-out entry. Login is a full navigation to `/api/auth/login`; the browser then holds only the API's `HttpOnly` session cookie, and the session's CSRF token stays in module memory for unsafe requests through the SDK. Sign-out clears all cached query data. `loginHref(returnTo, "strong" | "recent")` starts two-step verification when an operation answers `STRONG_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` or `RECENT_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`; the sessions page offers it directly. The navigation entry neither queries nor shows the session on `/docs` pages, so the portal still makes no API calls while browsing. Copy is localized through a typed pt-BR/en-US catalog in `src/identity/messages.ts`; no i18n library is selected yet. The API still verifies every business request, and production credentials must never be used in tests.
